class nanonis.command.CommandEncoder(debug: bool = False)

Encodes Python values to bytes for Nanonis protocol.

Supports: - Scalar types: float32, float64, int16, int32, uint16, uint32, bool - String: length-prefixed UTF-8 - 1D Arrays: array_float32, array_int32, array_string - 2D Arrays: matrix_float32, matrix_string

Features: - Automatic type coercion to prevent precision loss - Debug logging support

Encode multiple values according to their type definitions.

  • values – Tuple of values to encode

Returns:

Encoded bytes

class nanonis.command.CommandRegistry

Registry of all available Nanonis commands.

Loads command definitions from YAML and provides lookup.

Example

>>> registry = CommandRegistry()
>>> registry.load_from_yaml('configs/nanonis_tcp.yaml')
>>> cmd = registry.get('Bias.Set')
>>> print(cmd.send_args)

class nanonis.command.NanonisController(host: str, port: int, config_path: str | Path | None = None, timeout: float = 10.0, debug: bool = False)

Layer 2: Main command interface for Nanonis.

This is the primary entry point for sending commands to Nanonis. It combines the TCP client, command registry, and encoder/decoder.

Features: - Configuration-driven command dispatch - Automatic type coercion - Error detection from Nanonis responses - Debug mode for verbose logging

Example (standalone):
>>> with NanonisController('127.0.0.1', 6501, 'configs/nanonis_tcp.yaml') as ctrl:
...     ctrl.send('Bias.Set', 0.5)
...     voltage = ctrl.send('Bias.Get')
...     print(f"Bias: {voltage} V")
Example (with debug mode):
>>> ctrl = NanonisController('127.0.0.1', 6501, 'config.yaml')
>>> ctrl.debug = True  # Enable verbose logging
>>> ctrl.connect()
>>> ctrl.send('Bias.Get')

Nanonis Protocol Layer

Provides low-level TCP communication with the Nanonis controller.

exception nanonis.protocol.NanonisCommandError(command: str, message: str)

Raised when a command fails on the Nanonis side.

exception nanonis.protocol.NanonisConnectionError

Raised when connection to Nanonis fails.

exception nanonis.protocol.NanonisError

Base exception for all Nanonis-related errors.

exception nanonis.protocol.NanonisProtocolError

Raised when a protocol-level error occurs (malformed response, etc.).

class nanonis.protocol.NanonisTCPClient(host: str, port: int, timeout: float = 10.0)

Layer 1: Low-level TCP communication with Nanonis.

This class handles: - TCP socket connection management - Nanonis protocol header encoding (40 bytes) - Sending commands and receiving responses

Example

>>> with NanonisTCPClient('127.0.0.1', 6501) as client:
...     response = client.send_raw('Bias.Get', b'')
...     print(response)
connect() → None

Establish TCP connection to Nanonis.

Raises:

NanonisConnectionError – If connection fails

disconnect() → None

Close the TCP connection.

property is_connected: bool

Check if socket is connected.

send_raw(command_name: str, body: bytes) → bytes

Send a raw command to Nanonis and receive the response.

Parameters:

  • command_name – The Nanonis command name (e.g., ‘Bias.Get’)

  • body – The encoded command body bytes

Returns:

The response body bytes (excluding header)

Raises:

  • NanonisConnectionError – If not connected

  • NanonisProtocolError – If response is malformed

  • NanonisTimeoutError – If response times out

exception nanonis.protocol.NanonisTimeoutError

Raised when a command times out.

QCoDeS Integration

class nanonis.qcodes.instrument.NanonisInstrument(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any)

QCoDeS Instrument for Nanonis SPM controller.

This is Layer 3 of the architecture, providing QCoDeS integration on top of the NanonisController (Layer 2).

Submodules:

bias: BiasChannel for voltage control scan: ScanChannel for scan control

Example

>>> from nanonis.qcodes import NanonisInstrument
>>> from qcodes import Station, Measurement
>>>
>>> # Create instrument
>>> nanonis = NanonisInstrument(
...     'nanonis',
...     host='127.0.0.1',
...     port=6501,
...     config_path='configs/nanonis_tcp.yaml'
... )
>>>
>>> # Use QCoDeS parameters
>>> nanonis.bias.voltage(0.5)
>>> print(nanonis.bias.voltage())
>>>
>>> # Use in Station
>>> station = Station()
>>> station.add_component(nanonis)
>>>
>>> # Use in Measurement
>>> meas = Measurement()
>>> meas.register_parameter(nanonis.bias.voltage)
>>>
>>> # Direct Layer 2 access if needed
>>> nanonis.send('Custom.Command', arg1, arg2)
>>>
>>> # Clean up
>>> nanonis.close()
close() → None

Close the instrument and disconnect.

property controller: NanonisController

Access to underlying controller for advanced usage.

class nanonis.qcodes.channels.scan.ScanChannel(parent, name: str, controller)

QCoDeS channel for Nanonis Scan control.

Provides parameters and methods for controlling the scanner.

Parameters:

  • center_x – Scan center X position (m)

  • center_y – Scan center Y position (m)

  • width – Scan width (m)

  • height – Scan height (m)

  • angle – Scan angle (degrees)

Operations:

  • start: Start scanning

  • stop: Stop scanning

  • set_frame: Set all frame parameters at once

Example

>>> nanonis = NanonisInstrument('nanonis', '127.0.0.1', 6501, 'config.yaml')
>>> nanonis.scan.width(100e-9)  # Set 100nm scan width
>>> nanonis.scan.start()
ScanChannel.set_frame(center_x: float, center_y: float, width: float, height: float, angle: float = 0.0) → None

Set all scan frame parameters at once.

Parameters:

  • center_x – X position of scan center (m)

  • center_y – Y position of scan center (m)

  • width – Width of scan frame (m)

  • height – Height of scan frame (m)

  • angle – Rotation angle (degrees)

ScanChannel.start(direction: Literal['up', 'down'] = 'up') → None

Start scanning.

Parameters:

direction – Scan direction, ‘up’ or ‘down’

ScanChannel.stop() → None

Stop scanning.

ScanChannel.pause() → None

Pause scanning.
